gaps.sentence: Don't wake him — he has just ___ asleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Has just' is followed by the past participle: fallen.

gaps.sentence: I ___ it matters whether we leave at six or seven — the traffic will be terrible either way.
gaps.hint: think meaning believe is a state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Think' in the sense of 'believe' is a state verb, so the negative present simple is used: don't think.

gaps.sentence: This is the second time the printer ___ down this week.
gaps.explanation: 'This is the second time …' is followed by the present perfect.

gaps.sentence: When I got to the office, I realised I ___ my security pass.
gaps.hint: the forgetting happened before realising it
gaps.explanation: The forgetting happened before the past moment of realising, so the past perfect is needed: had forgotten.

gaps.sentence: I ___ her at a conference in 2019, but we did not start working together until last year.
gaps.hint: in 2019 pins a finished past time
gaps.explanation: 'In 2019' is a finished past time, so the past simple is required: met.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.

gaps.sentence: My back hurts because I ___ the garden all afternoon.
gaps.hint: all afternoon explains the present pain
gaps.explanation: A recent continuous activity with a visible present result takes the present perfect continuous: have been digging.

gaps.sentence: Prices ___ sharply over the last six months, and shoppers are feeling it.
gaps.hint: over the last six months leads to now
gaps.explanation: 'Over the last six months' is a period leading up to now, which takes the present perfect: have risen.
